headline: No documented interaction pathway; both agents are network-isolated and lack shared I/O surfaces, so pairwise risks are minimal.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection bridge is documented: agent_a has no I/O surfaces and agent_b also exposes no I/O surfaces, with both showing network_egress:none. Without a shared channel or parser path, one agent cannot inject instructions into the other.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing the other's raw text as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not add copy-paste or shared-message bridges.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No data-leakage pathway is evident because both profiles show data_classes_touched empty, network_egress:none, and no shared workspace or authenticated surface is described. The pairwise interaction is undocumented, so uncertainty is resolved conservatively but the available profile fields block the usual leakage routes.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted access to sensitive files or a shared workspace, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent gains network egress, outbound exfiltration pathways should be reassessed.
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of both agents' inputs.
requires-engineering: add access controls if shared storage is introduced.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Capability conflict is not supported by the profiles: both agents have network_egress:none, no write surfaces are listed, and concurrency_model/sandboxing are empty. With no overlapping mutable resource documented, there is no plausible write-write conflict to assess.
conditions: IF either agent is given filesystem, git, database, or OAuth write access to the same resource, conflict risk becomes plausible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locking-free mutable state, reassess this sub-risk.
mitigations: Document any future write scopes before enabling them.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error chain is not documented: agent_a is an awesome-list repository, not an action-taking agent, and agent_b is a docs/library project with no described automation or downstream authority. Without evidence that B consumes A's outputs as authoritative, the usual cascade pathway is absent.
conditions: IF agent_b is configured to treat agent_a's outputs as authoritative inputs, reassess for cascade risk.
IF either agent is connected to an action-taking workflow (email, commits, tickets), the blast radius changes.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on outputs.
Do not wire A directly into B's decision path.
requires-engineering: add verification checks if a pipeline is later created.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced: both agents are open-source, docs-only profiles with no data_classes_touched and no residency, certification, or retention fields indicating regulated-data handling. Because the relevant compliance dimensions are absent, there is no documented breach pathway to score.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced into either agent's workflow, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF residency, retention, or certification requirements are later specified, reassess against those constraints.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Record residency and retention requirements before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy checks if regulated data is later processed.
